questions.text:
अभिकथन (A): विटामिन D हमारे शरीर में संचित नहीं हो सकता है।
कारण (R): विटामिन D वसा में घुलनशील विटामिन है और मूत्र के माध्यम से शरीर से बाहर नहीं निकलता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Vitamin D cannot be stored in our body.
Reason (R): Vitamin D is fat soluble vitamin and is not excreted from the body in urine.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given – one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option (C). The Assertion (A) is true — Vitamin D cannot be stored in the body. However, the Reason (R) is false. Vitamin D is indeed a fat-soluble vitamin, but that is exactly why it CAN be stored in fatty tissues and the liver. It is the water-soluble vitamins (like Vitamin C) that are excreted in urine and cannot be stored. Since Vitamin D is fat-soluble, it is NOT excreted in urine. The assertion is correct for a different reason: excess Vitamin D is actually stored in fat, but since its precursor synthesis depends on sunlight and dietary intake is limited, the body's capacity is restricted. The reason as stated contains a factual error by implying fat-soluble vitamins cannot be stored.

Assertion (A): Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis.
Reason (R): Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution reaction with the anion formed by phthalimide.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option (A). Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Gabriel Phthalimide synthesis works by the reaction of the phthalimide anion (a nucleophile) with an alkyl halide via SN2 reaction. Aryl halides (like chlorobenzene) have the C–X bond with partial double bond character due to resonance of the lone pair of the halogen with the benzene ring, making them highly resistant to nucleophilic attack. Since the phthalimide anion cannot displace the halide from aryl halides, aromatic primary amines cannot be synthesised by this method. Therefore, the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.

कारण (R): Cu इलेक्ट्रोड विभव धनात्मक है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Cu cannot liberate H2 on reaction with dilute mineral acids.
Reason (R): Cu has positive electrode potential.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option (A). Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. A metal can displace hydrogen from dilute acids only if its standard electrode potential is negative (i.e., it lies above hydrogen in the electrochemical series). Copper has a positive standard electrode potential (E° = +0.34 V), which means it is less reactive than hydrogen and cannot reduce H+ ions from dilute acids to liberate H2 gas. Therefore, the positive electrode potential of Cu is the correct reason why it cannot liberate hydrogen from dilute mineral acids.

Reason (R): The half-life of a reaction does not depend upon the initial concentration of the reactant in a first order reaction.

options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option (D). The Assertion (A) is FALSE, but the Reason (R) is TRUE. For a first order reaction, the half-life is given by t1/2 = 0.693/k, which is independent of the initial concentration of the reactant. Therefore, if the concentration is doubled, the half-life remains the same — it does NOT double. So the Assertion is incorrect. The Reason, however, is a correct and true statement about first order kinetics. Hence option (D) is correct.

questions.text: स्कर्वी रोग किसकी कमी के कारण होता है?
questions.text_english: Scurvy is caused due to deficiency of
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (C) Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C). Scurvy is a disease caused by the deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid), which is essential for the synthesis of collagen. Symptoms include bleeding gums, skin lesions, and poor wound healing. Vitamin B1 deficiency causes Beriberi, Vitamin B2 deficiency causes Ariboflavinosis, and Glutamic acid is an amino acid, not a vitamin.

questions.text: न्यूक्लियोटाइड आपस में किस बंध द्वारा जुड़े होते हैं?
questions.text_english: Nucleotides are joined together by
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (D) Phosphodiester linkage. In a nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) chain, individual nucleotides are covalently joined to each other through phosphodiester bonds, which are formed between the phosphate group of one nucleotide and the 3'-OH group of the sugar of the adjacent nucleotide. Glycosidic linkage joins the nitrogenous base to the sugar within a nucleotide. Peptide bonds link amino acids in proteins, and hydrogen bonds hold the two strands of DNA together.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा/से प्रोटीन के विकृतीकरण का उदाहरण है/हैं?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is/are examples of denaturation of protein?
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (D) Both (A) and (B). Denaturation of protein refers to the disruption of secondary and tertiary structure of the protein without breaking peptide bonds. Coagulation of egg white on heating is a classic example of denaturation, as the albumin protein loses its native structure. Curdling of milk (due to acid from bacteria) is also a form of denaturation of the casein protein. Clotting of blood, however, is an enzymatic cascade process (not simple denaturation) involving the conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin. Hence both (A) and (B) are correct examples.

questions.text: फीनॉल का सैलिसिलिक अम्ल में रूपांतरण निम्न में से किसके द्वारा किया जा सकता है?
questions.text_english: The conversion of phenol to salicylic acid can be accomplished by
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (C) Kolbe reaction. In the Kolbe reaction (also called Kolbe-Schmitt reaction), sodium phenoxide is treated with CO2 under pressure at 400 K, followed by acidification to yield salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). The Reimer-Tiemann reaction converts phenol to salicylaldehyde (not salicylic acid). Friedel-Crafts reaction involves acylation or alkylation, and coupling reaction involves diazonium salts. Therefore, the Kolbe reaction is the correct answer.
questions.topic: Chemical Reactions of Phenols - Kolbe Reaction

questions.text: द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉल की क्रोमिक ऐनहाइड्राइड (CrO3) के साथ ऑक्सीकरण अभिक्रिया के बाद क्या बनेगा?
questions.text_english: What will be formed after oxidation reaction of secondary alcohol with chromic anhydride (CrO3)?
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (B) Ketone. Oxidation of a secondary alcohol with CrO3 (chromic anhydride) produces a ketone. Secondary alcohols have the hydroxyl group attached to a carbon that is bonded to two other carbon atoms. Upon oxidation, the –OH group is converted to a carbonyl group (C=O) flanked by two carbon groups, giving a ketone. Primary alcohols give aldehydes (which may be further oxidised to carboxylic acids), while secondary alcohols stop at the ketone stage since there is no alpha hydrogen on the other side for further oxidation.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कौन सा सही IUPAC नाम है? (बेंजीन वलय पर CH3 ऊपर और Cl नीचे, para स्थिति में)
questions.text_english: Which is the correct IUPAC name for the compound shown (benzene ring with CH3 at top and Cl at bottom in para position)?
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (C) 1-Chloro-4-Methylbenzene. In IUPAC nomenclature, when two substituents are on a benzene ring, numbering is done to give the lowest possible locants to the substituents. The principal characteristic group or the group that comes first alphabetically gets the lower number. Alphabetically, 'Chloro' comes before 'Methyl', so Cl gets position 1 and CH3 gets position 4. This gives 1-Chloro-4-Methylbenzene. Option (D) gives position 1 to methyl and 4 to chloro, which does not follow alphabetical priority in IUPAC naming.

questions.text: प्रतिचुंबकीय स्पीशीज़ है [परमाणु संख्या: Co = 27, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.text_english: The diamagnetic species is : [At. No. Co = 27, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (A) [Ni(CN)4]2-. Ni in this complex is Ni2+ (d8). CN- is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of all electrons, resulting in a square planar geometry with no unpaired electrons (t2g6 eg0 effectively for square planar d8). Hence it is diamagnetic. In [NiCl4]2-, Cl- is a weak field ligand, so Ni2+ retains 2 unpaired electrons (tetrahedral, paramagnetic). In [Fe(CN)6]3-, Fe3+ is d5, and even with strong field CN-, one electron remains unpaired (t2g5), making it paramagnetic. In [CoF6]3-, F- is weak field, Co3+ d6 has 4 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic.

questions.text: संकुल आयन [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]2+ तथा [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]2+ कहलाते हैं
questions.text_english: The complex ions [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]2+ and [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]2+ are called
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (B) Linkage isomers. These two complexes have the same molecular formula but differ in the mode of attachment of the ambidentate ligand NO2-. In [Co(NH3)5(NO2)]2+, the nitro ligand is bonded through nitrogen (–NO2), while in [Co(NH3)5(ONO)]2+, it is bonded through oxygen (–ONO, nitrito). Such isomers that differ only in the atom through which the ligand is coordinated to the central metal ion are called linkage isomers.

questions.text: [Ar]3d10 4s1 इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास वाला तत्व है
questions.text_english: The element having [Ar]3d10 4s1 electronic configuration is
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (A) Cu (Copper). Copper (Z = 29) has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d10 4s1, which is an exception to the aufbau principle. Instead of the expected [Ar]3d9 4s2, copper adopts [Ar]3d10 4s1 because a completely filled d-subshell (d10) is more stable. Zinc has [Ar]3d10 4s2, Chromium has [Ar]3d5 4s1, and Manganese has [Ar]3d5 4s2. Hence Cu is the correct answer.

questions.text: अणुओं की संख्या जो किसी प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया में परस्पर अभिक्रिया करते हैं, एक माप होती है
questions.text_english: The number of molecules that react with each other in an elementary reaction is a measure of the :
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (C) molecularity of the reaction. The molecularity of a reaction is defined as the number of reacting species (atoms, ions, or molecules) that come together and collide simultaneously in an elementary reaction. It is always a whole number and is defined only for elementary reactions. The order of a reaction is determined experimentally from the rate law and may be fractional or zero. Stoichiometry refers to the mole ratios in a balanced equation, and activation energy is the minimum energy required for the reaction.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन गलत है?
questions.text_english: Which among the following is a false statement?

options.A: शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया वेग अभिकारक की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता से स्वतंत्र होता है।
options.B: शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया की अर्द्ध-आयु, वेग स्थिरांक के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।
options.C: किसी अभिक्रिया की आण्विकता शून्य हो सकती है।
options.D: प्रथम कोटि अभिक्रिया के लिए t1/2 = 0.693/k

options_english.A: Rate of zero order reaction is independent of initial concentration of reactant.
options_english.B: Half-life of a zero order reaction is inversely proportional to the rate constant.
options_english.C: Molecularity of a reaction may be zero.
options_english.D: For a first order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option (C). The statement 'Molecularity of a reaction may be zero' is FALSE. Molecularity is the number of molecules participating in an elementary step; it is always a positive integer (1, 2, or rarely 3) and can never be zero or fractional. Statement (A) is true — rate of zero order = k, independent of concentration. Statement (B) is true — for zero order, t1/2 = [A]0/2k, i.e., inversely proportional to k. Statement (D) is true — for first order, t1/2 = 0.693/k.

questions.text: 1 मोल MnO4- को MnO2 में अपचयित करने के लिए आवश्यक आवेश है
questions.text_english: The charge required for the reduction of 1 mol of MnO4- to MnO2 is
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (B) 3 F. In MnO4-, Mn is in +7 oxidation state. In MnO2, Mn is in +4 oxidation state. The change in oxidation state = 7 - 4 = 3. Therefore, each mole of MnO4- requires 3 moles of electrons (3 Faradays of charge) for reduction to MnO2. The half-reaction is: MnO4- + 3e- + 2H2O → MnO2 + 4OH-. Hence, 3 F of charge is required per mole.

sub_questions.text: हैलोजन यौगिकों के निम्नलिखित युगल में से कौन सा यौगिक तीव्रता से SN1 अभिक्रिया करेगा और क्यों? (tertiary chloride और secondary chloride के संरचना चित्र दिए हैं)
sub_questions.text_english: In the following pair of halogen compounds, which compound undergoes SN1 reaction faster and why? (A tertiary chloride and a secondary chloride are shown)

key_points: Tertiary chloride undergoes SN1 faster
SN1 proceeds via carbocation intermediate
Tertiary carbocations are more stable due to +I effect of three alkyl groups

sub_questions.solution: The tertiary chloride (left compound) undergoes SN1 reaction faster. The SN1 mechanism involves the formation of a carbocation intermediate in the rate-determining step. A tertiary carbocation is more stable than a secondary carbocation because three alkyl groups attached to the positively charged carbon donate electrons through the +I (inductive) effect, effectively dispersing the positive charge. Greater the stability of the carbocation intermediate, faster is the rate of SN1 reaction. Hence, the tertiary chloride reacts much faster via SN1.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को SN2 प्रतिस्थापन के प्रति उनकी अभिक्रियाशीलता के बढ़ते क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए: 2-ब्रोमो-2-मेथिलब्यूटेन, 1-ब्रोमोपेन्टेन, 2-ब्रोमोपेन्टेन
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards SN2 displacement: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane, 1-Bromopentane, 2-Bromopentane.

key_points: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane < 2-Bromopentane < 1-Bromopentane
SN2 is hindered by steric bulk around the reaction centre

sub_questions.solution: The increasing order of reactivity towards SN2 displacement is: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane < 2-Bromopentane < 1-Bromopentane. The SN2 mechanism requires a backside attack by the nucleophile on the carbon bearing the leaving group. Steric hindrance around that carbon slows down the reaction. 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is tertiary and has the most steric hindrance, so it is least reactive. 2-Bromopentane is secondary and moderately hindered. 1-Bromopentane is primary and least hindered, so it reacts fastest in SN2.

questions.text: कोई अभिक्रिया अभिकारक के संबंध में द्वितीय कोटि की है। अभिक्रिया का वेग कैसे प्रभावित होगा; यदि अभिकारक की सांद्रता (i) दुगुनी कर दी जाए (ii) आधी कर दी जाए?
questions.text_english: A reaction is of second order with respect to a reactant. How is the rate of reaction affected if the concentration of the reactant is (i) doubled (ii) reduced to half?

key_points: Rate = k[A]^2 for second order reaction
When [A] doubled, rate becomes 4 times
When [A] halved, rate becomes 1/4 times

questions.solution: For a second order reaction, Rate = k[A]2. (i) When the concentration of the reactant is doubled: New Rate = k(2[A])2 = 4k[A]2 = 4 times the original rate. So the rate becomes four times. (ii) When the concentration is reduced to half: New Rate = k([A]/2)2 = k[A]2/4 = one-fourth of the original rate. So the rate becomes one-fourth.
questions.topic: Rate Law and Order of Reaction

questions.text: जब FeCr2O4 को वायु की उपस्थिति में Na2CO3 के साथ संगलित किया जाता है, तो यह यौगिक (A) का पीला विलयन देता है। यौगिक (A) अम्लीकृत होने पर यौगिक (B) देता है। यौगिक (B) KCl के साथ अभिक्रिया करके नारंगी रंग का यौगिक (C) बनाता है। यौगिक (C) का अम्लीय विलयन Na2SO3 को (D) में ऑक्सीकृत करता है। (A), (B), (C) और (D) को पहचानिए।
questions.text_english: When FeCr2O4 is fused with Na2CO3 in the presence of air it gives a yellow solution of compound (A). Compound (A) on acidification gives compound (B). Compound (B) on reaction with KCl forms an orange coloured (C). An acidified solution of compound (C) oxidises Na2SO3 to (D). Identify (A), (B), (C) and (D).

key_points: (A) = Na2CrO4 (Sodium chromate, yellow)
(B) = Na2Cr2O7 (Sodium dichromate, orange-red)
(C) = K2Cr2O7 (Potassium dichromate, orange)
(D) = Na2SO4 (Sodium sulphate)

questions.solution: When FeCr2O4 is fused with Na2CO3 in air, chromium is oxidised to Cr6+ forming (A) = Na2CrO4 (sodium chromate), which gives a yellow solution. On acidification, two CrO42- ions combine to form (B) = Na2Cr2O7 (sodium dichromate). Reaction of Na2Cr2O7 with KCl gives (C) = K2Cr2O7 (potassium dichromate), which is orange coloured. Acidified K2Cr2O7 is a strong oxidising agent and oxidises Na2SO3 (sodium sulphite, S = +4) to (D) = Na2SO4 (sodium sulphate, S = +6), while Cr6+ is reduced to Cr3+.

questions.text: समझाइए कि [Co(NH3)6]3+ एक आंतरिक कक्षक संकुल है जबकि [Ni(NH3)6]2+ एक बाह्य कक्षक संकुल है। [परमाणु संख्या: Co = 27, Ni = 28]
questions.text_english: Explain [Co(NH3)6]3+ is an inner orbital complex whereas [Ni(NH3)6]2+ is an outer orbital complex. [At. No. Co = 27, Ni = 28]

key_points: Co3+ is d6, with strong field NH3, electrons pair up in t2g leaving 3d, 4s, 4p orbitals for hybridisation (d2sp3 = inner orbital)
Ni2+ is d8, even with NH3, 3d orbitals are not empty enough; sp3d2 hybridisation uses 4d (outer orbital complex)

questions.solution: Co (Z=27) has configuration [Ar]3d7 4s2. As Co3+, it is [Ar]3d6. NH3 is a strong field ligand, so it causes pairing of all six 3d electrons into the three lower t2g orbitals, leaving two empty 3d orbitals. These empty 3d orbitals along with one 4s and three 4p orbitals undergo d2sp3 hybridisation (inner d orbitals used), forming an inner orbital complex. Ni (Z=28) as Ni2+ is [Ar]3d8. Even with NH3, the 3d subshell cannot be vacated as d8 configuration means all five 3d orbitals have at least one electron. Therefore, hybridisation involves 4s, 4p and 4d orbitals (sp3d2), using outer d orbitals, making it an outer orbital complex.

sub_questions.text: शून्य कोटि की अभिक्रिया A → P के लिए वेग स्थिरांक 0.0030 mol L-1s-1 है। A की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता 0.10 M से 0.075 M तक रह जाने में कितना समय लगेगा?
sub_questions.text_english: The rate constant for a zero order reaction A → P is 0.0030 mol L-1s-1. How long will it take for the initial concentration of A to fall from 0.10 M to 0.075 M?
sub_questions.solution: For a zero order reaction, the integrated rate law is: [A]t = [A]0 - kt, which gives t = ([A]0 - [A]t) / k. Here, [A]0 = 0.10 M, [A]t = 0.075 M, and k = 0.0030 mol L-1s-1. Therefore, t = (0.10 - 0.075) / 0.0030 = 0.025 / 0.0030 = 8.33 seconds.

key_points: Rate of decomposition of NH3 = k = 2.5 × 10-4 mol L-1s-1
Rate of production of N2 = k/2 = 1.25 × 10-4 mol L-1s-1
Rate of production of H2 = 3k/2 = 7.5 × 10-4 mol L-1s-1

Rate of formation of N2 = k/2 = 2.5 × 10-4 / 2 = 1.25 × 10-4 mol L-1s-1. Rate of formation of H2 = 3k/2 = 3 × 2.5 × 10-4 / 2 = 3.75 × 10-4 mol L-1s-1.

questions.text: जल में प्रति लीटर 15 ग्राम यूरिया (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 60 g mol-1) वाले विलयन का परासरण दाब जल में ग्लूकोज़ (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 180 g mol-1) के विलयन के समान (आइसोटोनिक) है। इसके एक लीटर में उपस्थित ग्लूकोज़ के द्रव्यमान का परिकलन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A solution containing 15 g urea (molar mass = 60 g mol-1) per litre of solution in water has the same osmotic pressure (isotonic) as a solution of glucose (molar mass = 180 g mol-1) in water. Calculate the mass of glucose present in one litre of its solution.

key_points: For isotonic solutions, molar concentrations are equal
Moles of urea = 15/60 = 0.25 mol/L
Moles of glucose = 0.25 mol/L
Mass of glucose = 0.25 × 180 = 45 g

questions.solution: Two solutions are isotonic (have the same osmotic pressure) when their molar concentrations (molarities) are equal at the same temperature, because osmotic pressure π = MRT. Moles of urea in 1 L = 15 g / 60 g mol-1 = 0.25 mol. Since the two solutions are isotonic, the molarity of the glucose solution must also be 0.25 mol L-1. Therefore, mass of glucose in 1 litre = 0.25 mol × 180 g mol-1 = 45 g.

questions.text:
एसीटिक अम्ल के लिए Λ°m और इसकी वियोजन मात्रा (α) की गणना करें यदि इसकी मोलर चालकता 48.1 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1 है।
दिया गया है:
Λ°m (HCl) = 426 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1
Λ°m (NaCl) = 126 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1
Λ°m (CH3COONa) = 91 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1
questions.text_english:
Calculate Λ°m for acetic acid and its degree of dissociation (α) if its molar conductivity is 48.1 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1.
Given that:
Λ°m (HCl) = 426 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1
Λ°m (NaCl) = 126 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1
Λ°m (CH3COONa) = 91 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1

key_points: Λ°m(CH3COOH) = Λ°m(HCl) + Λ°m(CH3COONa) - Λ°m(NaCl) = 426 + 91 - 126 = 391 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1

questions.solution: Using Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions: Λ°m(CH3COOH) = Λ°m(HCl) + Λ°m(CH3COONa) - Λ°m(NaCl) = 426 + 91 - 126 = 391 Ω-1 cm2 mol-1. The degree of dissociation α = Λm / Λ°m = 48.1 / 391 = 0.123 (approximately 12.3%). This means at this concentration, about 12.3% of the acetic acid molecules are dissociated into ions.

sub_questions.text: d4 स्पीशीज़ में से Cr2+ प्रबल अपचायक है जबकि Mn3+ प्रबल ऑक्सीकारक है।
sub_questions.text_english: Of the d4 species, Cr2+ is strongly reducing while Mn3+ is strongly oxidising. Why?

key_points: Cr2+ (d4) tends to lose one more electron to achieve stable d3 (half-filled t2g) configuration, so it is a strong reducing agent
Mn3+ (d4) tends to gain one electron to achieve stable d5 (half-filled) configuration of Mn2+, so it is a strong oxidising agent

sub_questions.solution: Cr2+ has a d4 configuration. It tends to lose one more electron to attain the stable d3 (t2g3, half-filled t2g level) configuration of Cr3+. This tendency to get oxidised (lose electrons) makes Cr2+ a strong reducing agent. On the other hand, Mn3+ also has d4 configuration but it tends to gain one electron to attain the extra stable d5 (half-filled d-subshell) configuration of Mn2+. This tendency to gain electrons makes Mn3+ a strong oxidising agent.

sub_questions.text_english: Write two consequences of lanthanoid contraction.

key_points: Pairs of heavier transition metals (Zr/Hf, Nb/Ta, Mo/W) have almost identical radii and properties, making their separation difficult
Basic character of lanthanoid hydroxides decreases from La(OH)3 to Lu(OH)3

sub_questions.solution: Two consequences of lanthanoid contraction are: (1) The atomic and ionic radii of the elements of the third transition series (5d) are almost identical to those of the second transition series (4d) elements. For example, Zr and Hf, Nb and Ta have nearly the same radii, making them difficult to separate. (2) The basic strength of lanthanoid hydroxides decreases steadily from La(OH)3 (most basic) to Lu(OH)3 (least basic) across the lanthanoid series.

sub_questions.text_english: Which element of 3d series has lowest enthalpy of atomisation and why?

key_points: Zinc (Zn) has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation in the 3d series
Zn has d10s2 configuration with completely filled d-orbitals, so no d-electrons contribute to metallic bonding

sub_questions.solution: Zinc (Zn) has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation among the 3d series elements. Zinc has the electronic configuration [Ar]3d10 4s2. Since all d-orbitals are completely filled, there are no unpaired d-electrons available to contribute to metallic bonding. The metallic bond in zinc is therefore weak (formed only by 4s electrons), resulting in the lowest enthalpy of atomisation in the 3d series.

sub_questions.text_english:
Explain the following reactions and write chemical equation involved:
(a) Wolff-Kishner reduction
(b) Etard reaction
(c) Cannizzaro reaction

key_points: Wolff-Kishner: Carbonyl compound reduced to alkane using N2H4 and KOH/ethylene glycol
Etard: Toluene oxidised to benzaldehyde using CrO2Cl2
Cannizzaro: Aldehydes without alpha-H undergo disproportionation in conc. NaOH

sub_questions.solution: (a) Wolff-Kishner Reduction: A carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone) is treated with hydrazine (N2H4) to form a hydrazone, which on heating with KOH in ethylene glycol is reduced to the corresponding alkane with the loss of N2. For example, RCHO + N2H4 → RCH=N-NH2; then RCH=N-NH2 + KOH → RCH3 + N2. (b) Etard Reaction: Toluene (or an arene with a methyl group) is treated with chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) to give a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis yields benzaldehyde. C6H5CH3 + CrO2Cl2 → [complex] → C6H5CHO. (c) Cannizzaro Reaction: Aldehydes with no alpha-hydrogen (like formaldehyde or benzaldehyde) undergo self-oxidation-reduction (disproportionation) in concentrated NaOH. One molecule is oxidised to carboxylate salt and another is reduced to alcohol. 2C6H5CHO + NaOH → C6H5COO-Na+ + C6H5CH2OH.

(b) CH3CN --1.(DIBAL-H), 2.H2O--> A --तनु NaOH--> B --Δ--> C
sub_questions.text_english:
Write the structures of A, B and C in the following sequence of reactions:
(a) CH3COOH --SOCl2--> A --H2, Pd-BaSO4--> B --H2N-NH2--> C
(b) CH3CN --1.(DIBAL-H), 2. H2O--> A --Dil. NaOH--> B --heat--> C

key_points: (a) A = CH3COCl (Acetyl chloride), B = CH3CHO (Acetaldehyde), C = CH3CH=N-NH2 (Acetaldehyde hydrazone) or the Wolff-Kishner product ethane
(b) A = CH3CHO (Acetaldehyde), B = CH3CH(OH)CH(OH)CH3 or aldol product, C = CH3CH=CHCHO (Crotonaldehyde)

sub_questions.solution: (a) CH3COOH reacts with SOCl2 to give A = CH3COCl (acetyl chloride). A is then reduced using H2/Pd-BaSO4 (Rosenmund reduction) to give B = CH3CHO (acetaldehyde). B reacts with H2N-NH2 (hydrazine) to give C = CH3CH=N-NH2 (acetaldehyde hydrazone). (b) CH3CN is treated with DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride) followed by hydrolysis to give A = CH3CHO (acetaldehyde), as DIBAL-H reduces nitrile to aldehyde at -78°C. A undergoes aldol condensation with dilute NaOH to give B = CH3CH(OH)CH2CHO (3-hydroxybutanal, aldol product). On heating, B undergoes dehydration to give C = CH3CH=CHCHO (but-2-enal / crotonaldehyde).

sub_questions.text_english:
Define the following:
(i) Enantiomers
(ii) Racemic mixture

key_points: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images of each other
Racemic mixture is an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers showing no net optical rotation

sub_questions.solution: (i) Enantiomers: A pair of stereoisomers that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other are called enantiomers. They have identical physical properties (melting point, boiling point) but rotate the plane of polarised light in equal magnitudes but opposite directions (one is d/+ and the other is l/-). (ii) Racemic mixture: A racemic mixture (or racemate) is an equimolar mixture of two enantiomers of a chiral compound. It is optically inactive because the rotation caused by one enantiomer is exactly cancelled by the equal and opposite rotation caused by the other enantiomer.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is chlorobenzene resistant to nucleophilic substitution reaction?

key_points: Lone pair on Cl delocalises into benzene ring (resonance), giving C-Cl bond partial double bond character
C-Cl bond is shorter and stronger, harder to cleave

sub_questions.solution: Chlorobenzene is resistant to nucleophilic substitution because the lone pair of electrons on the chlorine atom is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance. This gives the C–Cl bond a partial double bond character, making it shorter and stronger than a normal C–Cl single bond (as in alkyl halides). As a result, it is difficult for a nucleophile to break this bond. Additionally, the electron-rich benzene ring repels incoming nucleophiles electrostatically.

sub_questions.solution: When D-glucose reacts with hydroxylamine (H2N–OH), the aldehyde group (–CHO) of glucose undergoes a nucleophilic addition–elimination reaction to form a glucose oxime: D-Glucose + H2N–OH → Glucose oxime (C6H12O6 → C6H13O5N) + H2O. sub_questions.text: ऐमीनो अम्ल उभयधर्मी व्यवहार दर्शाते हैं, क्यों?
sub_questions.text_english: Amino acids show amphoteric behaviour, why?

key_points: Amino acids contain both acidic -COOH and basic -NH2 groups
They can act as acids (donating H+ from -COOH) and as bases (accepting H+ on -NH2)
They exist as zwitterions in solution

sub_questions.solution: Amino acids show amphoteric behaviour because they contain both an acidic carboxyl group (–COOH) and a basic amino group (–NH2) in the same molecule. The –COOH group can donate a proton (acting as an acid), while the –NH2 group can accept a proton (acting as a base). In solution, amino acids exist as zwitterions (dipolar ions), where the –COOH loses a proton to the –NH2 group, forming –COO- and –NH3+. This dual nature allows them to react with both acids and bases.

sub_questions.text: विटामिन C हमारे शरीर में क्यों संचित नहीं हो सकता?
sub_questions.text_english: Why vitamin C cannot be stored in our body?

key_points: Vitamin C is water-soluble
Excess water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine and cannot be stored

sub_questions.solution: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a water-soluble vitamin. Water-soluble vitamins are not stored in the body because any excess amount is readily dissolved in blood and body fluids and is excreted through urine by the kidneys. Unlike fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) which can be stored in adipose tissue and liver, water-soluble vitamins must be regularly supplied through diet.

questions.text: ऐमीनों में नाइट्रोजन परमाणु पर एकाकी इलेक्ट्रॉन युग्म होता है जिसके कारण वे लुईस क्षारक की तरह व्यवहार करते हैं। Kb का मान जितना अधिक होगा या pKb का मान जितना कम होगा, क्षारक उतना ही प्रबल होगा। ऐल्कोहॉल, ईथर, एस्टर आदि की तुलना में ऐमीन अधिक क्षारकीय हैं। ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन का क्षारकीय गुण ऐल्किल प्रतिस्थापन की वृद्धि के साथ-साथ बढ़ना चाहिए। लेकिन यह नियमित रूप से नहीं होता है क्योंकि द्वितीयक ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन अप्रत्याशित रूप से जलीय विलयन में तृतीयक ऐमीन की तुलना में अधिक क्षारकीय होता है। ऐरोमैटिक ऐमीन अमोनिया और ऐलिफैटिक ऐमीन की तुलना में दुर्बल क्षारक होते हैं। इलेक्ट्रॉन मुक्त करने वाले समूह जैसे – CH3, –OCH3, –NH2 आदि, क्षारकीयता को बढ़ाते हैं जबकि इलेक्ट्रॉन खींचने (अपनयन) वाले प्रतिस्थापित समूह जैसे – NO2, –CN, हैलोजन आदि, ऐमीन की क्षारकीयता को कम करते हैं। इन प्रतिस्थापनों का प्रभाव m- स्थितियों की तुलना में p- पर अधिक होता है।
questions.text_english: Amines have a lone pair of electrons on nitrogen atom due to which they behave as Lewis base. Greater the value of Kb or smaller the value of pKb, stronger is the base. Amines are more basic than alcohols, ethers, esters, etc. The basic character of aliphatic amines should increase with the increase of alkyl substitution. But it does not occur in a regular manner as a secondary aliphatic amine is unexpectedly more basic than a tertiary amine in aqueous solutions. Aromatic amines are weaker bases than ammonia and aliphatic amines. Electron releasing groups such as -CH3, -OCH3, -NH2, etc., increase the basicity while electron-withdrawing substituents such as -NO2, -CN, halogens etc., decrease the basicity of amines. The effect of these substitute is more at p- than at m- position.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित को उनके क्षारकीय गुणों के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए। कारण दीजिए। (aniline, 4-nitroaniline, 4-methylaniline के संरचना चित्र दिए हैं)
sub_questions.text_english: Arrange the following in the increasing order of their basic character. Give reason: (structures of aniline, 4-nitroaniline with NO2 group, and 4-methylaniline with CH3 group are shown)
sub_questions.image_description: Structural formulas of three aromatic amines: aniline (C6H5NH2), 2,4-dinitroaniline or 4-nitroaniline (with NO2 substituent on ring), and 4-methylaniline (with CH3 substituent on ring).

key_points: 4-Nitroaniline < Aniline < 4-Methylaniline
NO2 is electron-withdrawing, decreases basicity; CH3 is electron-donating, increases basicity

sub_questions.solution: The increasing order of basic character is: 4-Nitroaniline < Aniline < 4-Methylaniline. The basicity of aromatic amines depends on the electron density on nitrogen. In 4-nitroaniline, the –NO2 group at the para position is strongly electron-withdrawing; it withdraws electron density from the ring and from the nitrogen through resonance, making the lone pair on N less available for protonation — hence it is least basic. In aniline, the lone pair is partially delocalised into the ring, reducing basicity compared to aliphatic amines. In 4-methylaniline, the –CH3 group donates electrons (+I effect), increasing electron density on N, making it the most basic of the three.

sub_questions.text: मेथिलऐमीन की तुलना में ऐनिलीन का pKb मान अधिक क्यों होता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Why pKb of aniline is more than that of methylamine?

key_points: In aniline, lone pair on N delocalises into benzene ring by resonance, reducing availability for protonation
In methylamine, +I effect of CH3 increases electron density on N, making it more basic

sub_questions.solution: The pKb of aniline is more (weaker base) than that of methylamine because in aniline, the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance. This reduces the availability of the lone pair for accepting a proton (H+), making aniline a weaker base. In methylamine, the methyl group donates electrons through the +I (inductive) effect, increasing the electron density on nitrogen and making the lone pair more readily available for protonation. Hence methylamine is a stronger base (lower pKb) than aniline.

key_points: (i) Increasing order: (CH3)3N < NH3 < CH3NH2 < (CH3)2NH
(ii) Ammonolysis gives a mixture of primary, secondary, and tertiary amines and quaternary ammonium salt, making separation of pure amine difficult

sub_questions.solution: (c)(i) The increasing order of basic character in aqueous solution is: (CH3)3N < NH3 < CH3NH2 < (CH3)2NH. In aqueous solution, the basicity depends on the stability of the protonated form (ammonium ion) through solvation by water. Secondary amine (CH3)2NH is most basic because the two methyl groups provide enough electron density on N, and the protonated form is stabilised by hydrogen bonding with water. Trimethylamine (CH3)3N is least basic among methylamines because the bulky methyl groups hinder solvation of the resulting (CH3)3NH+ ion. (c)(ii) Ammonolysis of alkyl halides is not a good method to prepare pure amines because the reaction is uncontrollable. The primary amine initially formed acts as a nucleophile and reacts further with the alkyl halide to give secondary amine, then tertiary amine, and finally a quaternary ammonium salt. The product is thus always a mixture, and separation of a single pure amine is very difficult.

questions.text: शुद्ध विलायक से विलयन में अथवा तनु विलयन से सांद्र विलयन में अर्धपारगम्य झिल्ली के माध्यम से विलायक का स्वतः प्रवर्तित प्रवाह परासरण कहलाता है। परासरण परिघटना को एक ही आकार के दो अंडों को लेकर प्रदर्शित किया जा सकता है। अंडे में खोल के नीचे और अंडे के पदार्थ के चारों ओर की झिल्ली अर्धपारगम्य होती है। अंडे को तनु हाइड्रोक्लोरिक अम्ल में डालकर बाहरी कठोर खोल को हटाया जा सकता है। कठोर खोल को हटाने के बाद एक अंडे को आसुत जल में और दूसरे को संतृप्त नमक के घोल में रखा जाता है। कुछ समय बाद, आसुत जल में रखा अंडा फूल जाता है, जबकि नमक के घोल में रखा अंडा सिकुड़ जाता है। परासरण को रोकने के लिए लगाया गया बाह्य दाब, परासरण दाब (एक अणुसंख्य गुणधर्म) कहलाता है। प्रतिलोम परासरण तब होता है जब लगाया गया बाह्य दाब परासरण दाब से अधिक हो जाता है।
questions.text_english: The spontaneous flow of the solvent through a semipermeable membrane from a pure solvent to a solution or from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution is called osmosis. The phenomenon of osmosis can be demonstrated by taking two eggs of the same size. In an egg, the membrane below the shell and around the egg material is semipermeable. The outer hard shell can be removed by putting the egg in dilute hydrochloric acid. After removing the hard shell, one egg is placed in distilled water and the other in a saturated salt solution. After some time, the egg placed in distilled water swells-up while the egg placed in salt solution shrinks. The external pressure applied to stop the osmosis is termed as osmotic pressure (a colligative property). Reverse osmosis takes place when the applied external pressure becomes larger than the osmotic pressure.

sub_questions.text_english: Define reverse osmosis. Name one SPM which can be used in the process of reverse osmosis.

key_points: Reverse osmosis: solvent flows from solution to pure solvent when applied pressure exceeds osmotic pressure
Cellulose acetate membrane is one SPM used

sub_questions.solution: Reverse osmosis is the process in which the solvent flows from a solution through a semipermeable membrane into the pure solvent (opposite to normal osmosis) when an external pressure greater than the osmotic pressure is applied on the solution side. It is used for the desalination of sea water to obtain fresh water. One semipermeable membrane used in reverse osmosis is cellulose acetate membrane (cellophane).

sub_questions.text: जब लाल रुधिर कोशिकाओं (RBC) को 0.5% NaCl विलयन में रखा जाता है तो आप क्या होने की अपेक्षा करते हैं?
sub_questions.text_english: What do you expect to happen when red blood corpuscles (RBC's) are placed in 0.5% NaCl solution?

key_points: 0.5% NaCl is hypotonic relative to blood (0.9%)
Water enters RBC by osmosis, cells swell and may burst (haemolysis)

sub_questions.solution: Normal blood plasma is isotonic with 0.9% NaCl solution. A 0.5% NaCl solution is hypotonic compared to blood. When RBCs are placed in 0.5% NaCl, the external solution has a lower solute concentration (lower osmotic pressure) than the cell fluid. Consequently, water moves into the RBC by osmosis, causing the cells to swell up. If placed for too long, the cells may burst — a process called haemolysis.

sub_questions.text: 1 M KCl अथवा 1 M यूरिया विलयन में से किसका परासरण दाब अधिक होगा। अपने उत्तर का औचित्य दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following will have higher osmotic pressure in 1 M KCl or 1 M urea solution. Justify your answer.

key_points: 1 M KCl has higher osmotic pressure
KCl dissociates into K+ and Cl- giving 2 mol particles per mol, while urea (non-electrolyte) gives 1 mol particles

sub_questions.solution: 1 M KCl solution will have higher osmotic pressure than 1 M urea solution. This is because KCl is a strong electrolyte that completely dissociates: KCl → K+ + Cl-, giving 2 moles of particles per mole of KCl. Urea is a non-electrolyte and does not dissociate, giving only 1 mole of particles per mole. Since osmotic pressure π = iCRT, and the van't Hoff factor i = 2 for KCl versus i = 1 for urea, KCl has twice the effective particle concentration, hence higher osmotic pressure.

sub_questions.text_english: Why osmotic pressure is a colligative property?

key_points: Colligative properties depend only on number of solute particles, not their nature
Osmotic pressure depends on molar concentration (number of solute particles) not on identity of solute

sub_questions.solution: Osmotic pressure is a colligative property because it depends only on the number of solute particles (molar concentration) present in the solution and not on the nature or identity of the solute. The relationship π = CRT (or π = nRT/V) shows that osmotic pressure depends only on the molar concentration C, which is determined by the number of dissolved particles. Two solutions with the same molar concentration of any solute (same number of particles) will have the same osmotic pressure, regardless of the chemical nature of the solute.

sub_questions.text_english: An organic compound 'A', molecular formula C2H6O oxidises with CrO3 to form a compound 'B'. Compound 'B' on warming with iodine and aqueous solution of NaOH gives a yellow precipitate of compound 'C'. When compound 'A' is heated with conc. H2SO4 at 413 K gives a compound 'D', which on reaction with excess HI gives compound 'E'. Identify compounds 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D' and 'E' and write chemical equations involved.

key_points: A = Ethanol (CH3CH2OH)
B = Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO)
C = Iodoform (CHI3)
D = Diethyl ether (CH3CH2OCH2CH3)
E = Ethyl iodide (CH3CH2I)

sub_questions.solution: The molecular formula C2H6O can be ethanol (CH3CH2OH). Compound A = CH3CH2OH (Ethanol). Step 1: Ethanol oxidised with CrO3 gives B = CH3CHO (Acetaldehyde). CH3CH2OH + CrO3 → CH3CHO. Step 2: Acetaldehyde undergoes the iodoform reaction with I2/NaOH (aqueous) to give C = CHI3 (Iodoform, a yellow precipitate) and sodium acetate. CH3CHO + 3I2 + 3NaOH → CHI3 + CH3COONa + 3NaI + 3H2O. Step 3: When ethanol is heated with conc. H2SO4 at 413 K (140°C), intermolecular dehydration occurs to give D = CH3CH2OCH2CH3 (Diethyl ether). 2CH3CH2OH → CH3CH2OCH2CH3 + H2O. Step 4: Diethyl ether reacts with excess HI to give E = CH3CH2I (Ethyl iodide / Iodoethane). CH3CH2OCH2CH3 + 2HI → 2CH3CH2I + H2O.

sub_questions.text_english:
Write chemical equations of the following reactions:
(a) Phenol is treated with conc. HNO3
(b) Propene is treated with B2H6 followed by oxidation by H2O2/OH-.
(c) Sodium t-butoxide is treated with CH3Cl.
And:
(b) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol.
(c) Arrange the following in increasing order of acid strength: phenol, ethanol, water

key_points: Phenol + conc. HNO3 → 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid)
Propene + B2H6 then H2O2/OH- → propan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov addition)
Sodium t-butoxide + CH3Cl → Williamson synthesis giving methyl t-butyl ether
Butan-1-ol (primary) vs butan-2-ol (secondary) distinguished by Lucas test or oxidation with CrO3
Acid strength: Ethanol < Water < Phenol

sub_questions.solution: (a) Phenol treated with conc. HNO3 undergoes nitration to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid): C6H5OH + 3HNO3 (conc.) → C6H2(NO2)3OH + 3H2O. (b) Propene treated with B2H6 (hydroboration) followed by H2O2/OH- (oxidation) gives propan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov addition of water): CH3CH=CH2 + B2H6 → (CH3CH2CH2)3B → H2O2/OH- → CH3CH2CH2OH (propan-1-ol). (c) Sodium t-butoxide + CH3Cl (Williamson synthesis): (CH3)3CONa + CH3Cl → (CH3)3COCH3 (methyl t-butyl ether) + NaCl. For part (b) — to distinguish butan-1-ol (primary) from butan-2-ol (secondary), use the Lucas test: add anhydrous ZnCl2 and conc. HCl. Butan-2-ol (secondary) turns turbid almost immediately, while butan-1-ol (primary) takes a long time or requires heating. For part (c) — increasing order of acid strength: Ethanol < Water < Phenol. Phenol is most acidic because the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance with the benzene ring. Water is more acidic than ethanol because the electron-donating ethyl group in ethanol destabilises the ethoxide ion.

key_points: (a) CH3-CH=CH-CHO: IUPAC name = But-2-enal
(b) Propanal vs Propanone: Tollens' test / Fehling's test (propanal positive, propanone negative)
(c)(i) Toluene to benzoic acid: oxidation with KMnO4/H+
(c)(ii) Ethanol to propan-2-ol: conversion via Grignard reagent or through acetaldehyde
(c)(iii) Propanal to 2-hydroxy propanoic acid: reaction with HCN then hydrolysis

sub_questions.solution: (a) The IUPAC name of CH3-CH=CH-CHO is But-2-enal. The parent chain has 4 carbons. The aldehyde group (-CHO) gets the lowest locant (C1). The double bond is between C2 and C3, so it is but-2-en-1-al = But-2-enal. (b) To distinguish propanal from propanone: add Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate solution). Propanal (an aldehyde) is oxidised and gives a silver mirror (positive test). Propanone (a ketone) does not react with Tollens' reagent (negative test). Alternatively, Fehling's solution gives a brick-red precipitate with propanal but not with propanone. (c)(i) Toluene to Benzoic acid: Treat toluene (C6H5CH3) with acidified KMnO4 and heat. The methyl group is oxidised to –COOH, giving benzoic acid (C6H5COOH). (c)(ii) Ethanol to Propan-2-ol: First convert ethanol to acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) by oxidation with CrO3. Then treat acetaldehyde with CH3MgBr (Grignard reagent) followed by hydrolysis to get propan-2-ol (CH3CH(OH)CH3). (c)(iii) Propanal to 2-Hydroxypropanoic acid (Lactic acid): Treat propanal (CH3CH2CHO) with HCN to get cyanohydrin CH3CH2CH(OH)CN, then hydrolyse with dilute HCl/H2O to get 2-hydroxypropanoic acid (CH3CH(OH)COOH).

sub_questions.image_description: Five reaction scheme diagrams: (a) cyclopentanone reacting with hydroxylamine; (b) unknown starting material ozonolysis giving 2 equivalents of cyclopentanone; (c) cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid with SOCl2 and heat; (d) a cyclohexane compound with CHO and COOH groups reacting with NaCN/HCl; (e) benzene converting to acetophenone (phenyl methyl ketone).

key_points: (a) Product = cyclopentanone oxime
(b) Starting material = 1-cyclopentylidenecyclopentane (bicyclopentylidene)
(c) Product = cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic anhydride (cyclic anhydride)
(d) Product = 2-(cyanomethyl)cyclohexane carboxylic acid (cyanohydrin of aldehyde group added)
(e) Reagent = CH3COCl / AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts acylation)

sub_questions.solution: (a) Cyclopentanone reacts with hydroxylamine (HO-NH2) in acidic conditions to undergo nucleophilic addition-elimination, giving cyclopentanone oxime (the C=O is converted to C=N-OH). (b) Ozonolysis (O3, then Zn/H2O) of a compound gives 2 equivalents of cyclopentanone. Working backwards, the starting material must be 1,1'-bicyclopentylidene (two cyclopentane rings joined by a double bond, C=C), since ozonolysis of the C=C of this compound would give two cyclopentanone molecules. (c) Cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid treated with SOCl2 and heat undergoes intramolecular dehydration to give the cyclic anhydride — cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic anhydride (SOCl2 converts -OH of COOH to -Cl, and heating causes cyclisation with loss of HCl). (d) The compound with CHO and COOH on cyclohexane reacts with NaCN/HCl: HCN (generated from NaCN/HCl) adds to the aldehyde group (cyanohydrin formation), giving a product where the CHO is converted to CH(OH)CN (cyanohydrin), while the COOH group is unaffected. (e) To convert benzene to acetophenone (C6H5COCH3): use Friedel-Crafts acylation. Treat benzene with acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 (Lewis acid catalyst). C6H6 + CH3COCl → (AlCl3) → C6H5COCH3 + HCl.

key_points: (a) E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode; then ΔrG° = -nFE°cell
n = 6 (LCM of 3 and 2)
ΔrG° = -6 × 96500 × 4.37 = -2530410 J/mol (very negative, reaction is spontaneous)
(b) Tarnished silver: yes, tarnish can be removed; Al acts as anode and gets oxidised

sub_questions.solution: (a) The cell reaction is: Au(s) + Ca2+(1M) → Au3+(1M) + Ca(s). E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode. Here Au3+/Au is reduced (cathode), Ca2+/Ca is oxidised (anode). E°cell = E°(Au3+/Au) - E°(Ca2+/Ca) = (+1.5) - (-2.87) = +4.37 V. To balance electrons: Au → Au3+ + 3e- and Ca2+ + 2e- → Ca. LCM = 6, so n = 6. ΔrG° = -nFE°cell = -6 × 96500 × 4.37 = -2,530,410 J mol-1 = -2530.41 kJ mol-1. Since ΔrG° is large and negative, the reaction is spontaneous at 25°C. (b) Standard electrode potentials: Ag2S + 2e- → 2Ag + S2- (E° = -0.71 V) and Al3+ + 3e- → 2Al (E° = -1.66 V). The reduction potential of Al3+/Al is more negative than that of Ag2S/Ag. So Al is a stronger reducing agent and will reduce Ag2S, being itself oxidised to Al3+. The overall cell EMF = -0.71 - (-1.66) = +0.95 V (positive), confirming the reaction is feasible. Therefore, yes, the tarnish (Ag2S) CAN be removed by placing the silverware in an aluminium pan with NaCl solution, as Al reduces Ag2S back to Ag.

key_points: (a)(i) Cell potential: difference of electrode potentials of cathode and anode (EMF of the cell)
(a)(ii) Fuel cell: galvanic cell that converts chemical energy of fuel directly into electrical energy
(b) E°cell = E°Cd2+/Cd - E°Zn2+/Zn = -0.40 - (-0.76) = +0.36 V; apply Nernst equation

sub_questions.solution: (a)(i) Cell potential (EMF): The cell potential is the difference between the electrode potentials (reduction potentials) of the cathode and anode. It is the driving force that causes the flow of electrons in the external circuit. Ecell = Ecathode - Eanode. (a)(ii) Fuel cell: A fuel cell is an electrochemical device (galvanic cell) that converts the chemical energy of a fuel (such as hydrogen or methane) directly into electrical energy through redox reactions without combustion. For example, in a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell, H2 is oxidised at the anode and O2 is reduced at the cathode to produce water and electricity. (b) For the cell Zn(s)|Zn2+(0.1M)||Cd2+(0.01M)|Cd(s): E°cell = E°Cd2+/Cd - E°Zn2+/Zn = (-0.40) - (-0.76) = +0.36 V. Applying Nernst equation at 25°C: Ecell = E°cell - (0.0591/n) × log([Zn2+]/[Cd2+]) = 0.36 - (0.0591/2) × log(0.1/0.01) = 0.36 - (0.02955) × log(10) = 0.36 - 0.02955 × 1 = 0.36 - 0.02955 = 0.3305 V ≈ 0.33 V.
